projects.name: Toolly Scan
projects.summary: A modern Android toolkit for QR scanning and generation, document workflows, digital business cards, and secure local utilities.
projects.overview: Toolly combines QR scanning and generation, PDF tools, camera-driven document workflows, digital business cards, encryption, and background processing in one modular Android application.
projects.problem: Everyday capture and utility tasks often require several disconnected apps or cloud-first processing. Toolly explores a cohesive workflow that keeps useful data local wherever practical.
projects.role: Product direction, mobile architecture, Android implementation, quality strategy, and CI/CD.
approach: Design offline-first flows before introducing network dependencies.
Keep scanning and recognition work on-device where supported.
Model features as composable utilities sharing secure local foundations.
projects.architecture: A Kotlin and Jetpack Compose application using MVI and MVVM boundaries, Room for structured local data, DataStore for preferences, and encrypted local handling where sensitive information is involved.
decisions: Use ML Kit Document Scanner for device-native document capture.
Prefer local persistence and explicit data ownership.
Keep future Kotlin Multiplatform adoption as an architectural direction rather than a released capability claim.
challenges: Balancing a broad utility surface with a coherent, accessible navigation model.
Handling document and card information without weakening local privacy expectations.
projects.outcome: The public repository documents the modular architecture and active development roadmap. Release adoption and production-readiness are not claimed.

projects.name: DataLoom
projects.summary: A deterministic synchronisation SDK foundation for native Android and Kotlin Multiplatform applications targeting Android and iOS.
projects.overview: DataLoom is an Android-first, Jetpack-style SDK working toward six explicit synchronisation strategies: offline-first, remote-first, cache-first, network-only, hybrid, and adaptive.
projects.problem: Synchronisation logic is frequently scattered across repositories, workers, caches, queues, and retry code. DataLoom aims to make policy and runtime behaviour explicit, deterministic, and testable.
projects.role: SDK product direction, Kotlin architecture, contracts, runtime design, testing foundations, and documentation.
approach: Separate strategy policy from transfer direction, transfer mode, and triggers.
Keep application payloads opaque so domain truth stays with consumers.
Build durable recovery, deterministic planning, and observability as first-class systems.
projects.architecture: A modular Kotlin foundation spanning dependency-root models, public APIs, provider lifecycle, shared runtime orchestration, deterministic testing tools, Android adapters, Room-backed queues, WorkManager scheduling, and Apple compilation paths.
decisions: Publish versioned contracts for all six intended strategies before representing them as complete.
Keep provider resolution and orchestration modular across Android and KMP consumer paths.
Document explicit production-readiness gates and no-go conditions.
challenges: Durable decision persistence and several strategy runtimes remain incomplete.
Platform qualification, asset transfer, governance, and complete operational systems remain V1 gates.
projects.outcome: The public repository contains substantial foundations and direct network-only and remote-first slices, but its own documentation explicitly states that it is not production-ready and has no stable V1 release.

principles.title: Maintainable architecture
principles.description: Keep responsibilities and dependencies visible so teams can change behaviour without unravelling unrelated features.

principles.title: Clear state management
principles.description: Represent loading, content, empty, and failure states explicitly, with one understandable source of truth.

principles.title: Offline resilience
principles.description: Design useful behaviour for intermittent networks and make synchronisation decisions deliberate.

principles.title: Security by design
principles.description: Minimise sensitive data, secure local storage, use trusted platform APIs, and review boundaries early.

principles.title: Performance awareness
principles.description: Measure startup, rendering, memory, and ANR behaviour, then optimise the bottleneck that evidence identifies.

principles.title: Accessible by default
principles.description: Build semantics, focus, readable contrast, localisation, and adaptable interactions into the component system.

principles.title: Automated confidence
principles.description: Use focused unit, integration, and UI tests to protect important behaviour without slowing useful change.

principles.title: Observable delivery
principles.description: Make failures diagnosable through clear logging, operational signals, documentation, and reproducible builds.
